title: Herb-Crusted Rack of Lamb with a Mustard Layer
changes_from_base: A mustard paste made from mustard powder and seeds (no prepared mustard) is brushed on before the herb crumb; otherwise the same sear, crust and roast.
summary: This follows the classic persillade rack of lamb method, with one change: a homemade mustard paste of mustard powder, crushed seeds, lemon and honey is brushed on before the herb crumb. It adds a gentle heat and helps the crust grip the meat.
equipment: large ovenproof frying pan or cast-iron pan
wire rack set in a rimmed baking tray

ingredients.item: French-trimmed racks of lamb (7-8 bones, about 700 g each)
ingredients.note: fat trimmed to a thin layer

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Heat and season
steps.text: This version follows the classic persillade method, adding a mustard layer under the crumb. Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C), pat the racks dry and season all over with the lamb salt and pepper. Dry meat browns faster, giving more flavour in less time.

steps.title: Sear the racks
steps.text: Heat the oil in the pan over medium-high heat and brown each rack fat side down for 3-4 min, then 1 min on each other side, standing it up with tongs to colour the ends. Look for an even golden-brown surface; this browning gives the finished lamb its savoury depth.

steps.title: Rest on the rack
steps.text: Transfer the racks to the wire rack in the tray, fat side up, and cool for 5 min. A cooler surface lets both the mustard and the crumb stick rather than slip.

steps.title: Mix the mustard paste
steps.text: Stir the mustard powder, crushed seeds, lemon juice, water and honey together into a smooth paste. Leave it for 10 min to develop: mustard heat only appears once the powder has been wet for a few minutes.

steps.title: Brush and blitz
steps.text: Brush the paste over the fat side and ends of each seared rack. Next, blitz the parsley, rosemary, garlic and lemon zest in the processor until fine, then add the breadcrumbs, olive oil and crust salt and pulse to a bright green, damp crumb that clumps when squeezed.

steps.title: Coat the lamb
steps.text: Press the crumb firmly over the mustard layer in an even coat. The tacky paste acts like glue, so the crust holds together well when you carve.

steps.title: Roast, rest and carve
steps.text: Roast for 18-25 min, until a thermometer in the thickest part of the eye, not touching bone, reads at least 63°C. Cover loosely with foil if the crust darkens too soon. Rest for 5 min (at least 3 min), then cut between the bones into cutlets, serving 4 per person.

tips: Let the mustard paste stand the full 10 min; brushed on straight away, it tastes flat rather than warm.
A common mistake is brushing on too thick a mustard layer, which can make the crust slide; a thin, even coat is enough.
Crush the mustard seeds only lightly so they add little bursts of texture.
If the crust browns well before the lamb reaches temperature, foil protects it without slowing the roast much.
storage: Cool leftovers within 2 hours and keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in a hot oven until piping hot (74°C).
